newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian ex-justice minister defends Hass.
newsitem.headline: Italian ex-justice minister defends Hass.

text.p: Former Italian justice minister Giuliano Vassalli testified on Tuesday in the defence of Karl Hass and said the ex-SS major, accused of taking part in Italy's worst World War Two atrocity, had helped save his life.
Vassalli, a partisan who fought the Germans during the war, said Hass had been instrumental in delaying his death while he was a prisoner at the Gestapo's Rome headquarters in Via Tasso.

He told the court in Rome's high-security Rebibbia prison that his life had been spared in 1944 after Pope Pius XII indirectly contacted Hass through a series of intermediaries in an attempt to stop the execution.
"(Hass) asked the command of Via Tasso to interrogate me, and because of that my execution was delayed until June 3 when I was set free," Vassalli said.
Hass is on trial with Erich Priebke, a former SS captain accused in the same 1944 massacre of 335 men and boys, 75 of them Jews, at the Ardeatine Caves south of Rome.
Priebke, 83, was extradited from Argentina in November 1995 and is being re-tried after a court last August found him guilty but ordered he be set free under a statute of limitation.
The verdict, which sparked a storm of protest, was quashed on appeal and a retrial began in April this year. Hass is being tried for the first time.
Both men admit to having taken part in the massacre, but say they were following orders and would have been executed if they had refused to act.

Neither Priebke, who is under house arrest at a Roman Catholic monastery south of Rome, nor Hass was present at Tuesday's hearing. Under Italian law, defendants are not obliged to attend trial sessions.
